title: Sky Trial Sprint
premise: Guide a glowing pilot-like runner upward through layered airspace by timing jumps across floating platforms while the character auto-moves side to side.
interaction_model: One-button arcade control using tap/click on the canvas or Space to jump when grounded; start and restart are handled by button press or Space.
objective: Climb as high as possible, survive increasingly hostile airspace zones, and set a new best altitude before falling below the camera.
progression: Endless score-attack ascent with named altitude zones that increase difficulty by narrowing platforms, widening gaps, introducing moving platforms, and accelerating hero speed.
theme: Neon sci-fi aviation ascent through sky, storm, void, and starfield airspace layers.
mood: Energetic, futuristic, arcade-like, and tense as the climb becomes faster and less forgiving.
likely_audience: players who enjoy endless climbing or runner hybrids
confidence_notes: High confidence on the core loop, controls, progression, and presentation because they are explicit in the source code. Moderate uncertainty remains only around exact narrative framing of the avatar, which is visually abstract but described with pilot/plane language in the UI.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished single-screen arcade game called "Sky Trial Sprint" about a glowing neon pilot-runner climbing upward through layered airspace. The game should run on a fullscreen canvas with a sci-fi HUD and start/game-over overlays. The player controls only jumping: tap/click the playfield on mobile or press Space on keyboard to jump, and jumps are allowed only while the character is standing on a platform. The character should move horizontally on its own at constant speed, bounce off the left and right screen edges, and rely on player jump timing rather than direct steering. Build the main loop around a vertical survival ascent: gravity pulls the character down, floating platforms are generated upward above the camera, and the score represents altitude in meters. As the player climbs, promote them through named zones such as LOW SKY, JET STREAM, STORM EDGE, NIGHT VOID, STAR FIELD, and SOLAR GATE. Each new zone should shift the palette and increase difficulty by shrinking platform widths, increasing platform gaps, enabling moving platforms, and slightly increasing horizontal character speed. The run ends when the character falls below the camera view, then show a game-over panel with best altitude and last reached airspace plus a restart action. Present everything with bright neon gradients, glowing platforms, a compact glowing hero, subtle background stars and streaks, celebratory zone title popups, particles, screen shake on failure, and energetic audio for jump, landing, zone clear, UI start, fail, and looping background music. The overall feel should be a fast, readable, mobile-safe, one-button endless vertical platformer with auto-runner behavior and strong arcade feedback.
